    distmer

    A transparent, extensible R framework for distance-based fixed and mixed models (PERMANOVA-style) in ecological community analysis. Unsupported inference structures fail explicitly instead of receiving an implicit denominator or permutation scheme.

    Quick start

    permanova() is the main user interface. Give it an lmer-style formula with the dissimilarity on the left-hand side. It validates the sampling structure, matches the model to a supported distance-based inference method, and returns a familiar results table with a permutation p-value and, where applicable, a smooth Monte-Carlo P(MC).

    library(distmer)
data(dune, dune.env, package = "vegan")
bray <- vegan::vegdist(dune, method = "bray")

# one fixed factor (agrees with vegan::adonis2)
permanova(bray ~ Management, dune.env, permutations = 999, seed = 1)

# unbalanced fixed factors, Type II sums of squares
permanova(bray ~ Management + Moisture, dune.env, type = "II")

# one random intercept (whole-plot EMS denominator)
permanova(bray ~ treatment + (1 | site), sampling_design)

# split-plot / RCB ANCOVA (covariate adjusted)
permanova(bray ~ treatment + volume + (1 | site), sampling_design)

# nested hierarchy, covariate-adjusted nested strata, crossed/randomized block,
# crossed-nested hybrid, random slopes -- all through the same call:
permanova(bray ~ treatment + (1 | region/site), sampling_design)
permanova(bray ~ x + (1 + x | group), sampling_design)

    The selected implementation is printed in the header and stored in fit$engine; its detailed result is in fit$fit, and summary(fit) adds estimates of components of variation. Designs outside every supported envelope stop with a message naming the reason rather than guessing a denominator.

    Advanced users can compile a design explicitly with compile_permanova_design() and call a specialised function when they need a low-level argument. For example, permanova_dispersion() and the contrast families take a compiled design. In day-to-day use, start with permanova().

    Balanced random-intercept inference 

    fit <- permanova(bray ~ treatment + (1 | site), sampling_design,
                 permutations = 9999, seed = 5)
fit$fit$tests$treatment$symbolic_ems

    Use permutations = "all" for exhaustive enumeration when the whole-plot permutation space does not exceed max_exact.

    Balanced crossed mixed inference

    Phase 3 supports complete, equally replicated factorial designs whose fixed-by-random covariance components are declared explicitly:

    design <- compile_permanova_design(
  ~ treatment +
    (1 | block) + (1 | observer) +
    (1 | treatment:block) + (1 | treatment:observer),
  data = sampling_design,
  distance = community_distance
)

fit <- permanova_crossed(design)
fit$variance_components$unrestricted

    Trace-derived EMS coefficients select and pool exact orthogonal denominator strata. quasi_denominator() constructs an EMS-matched linear combination when no single exact stratum exists. Negative unrestricted variance components are retained; request truncate = TRUE to report a separate zero-truncated sensitivity result. Parametric Satterthwaite p-values are never implicit and require p_method = "satterthwaite"; they are suppressed for non-Euclidean dissimilarities. Omitted fixed-by-random components fail by default. The assume_additive = TRUE escape hatch is an explicit zero-variance assumption, recorded with the pooled denominator strata in every Test Specification.

    The canonical randomized-block model also has a permutation path:

    design <- compile_permanova_design(
  ~ treatment + (1 | block) + (1 | treatment:block),
  data = sampling_design,
  distance = community_distance
)

fit <- permanova_crossed(
  design,
  p_method = "permutation",
  permutations = 9999,
  seed = 5
)

    Complete replicated treatment cells move among treatment positions within each block. Use permutations = "all" when (treatments!)^blocks does not exceed max_exact. This empirical path supports retained non-Euclidean distances. Additional fixed/random factors, nesting, imbalance, or additive omissions remain explicit failures for permutation inference.

    Balanced nested mixed inference 

    fit <- permanova(
  community_distance ~ region_treatment + site_treatment +
    observation_treatment + (1 | region/site),
  sampling_design, permutations = 9999, seed = 5
)
fit$fit$assignment_levels
fit$fit$tests$site_treatment$symbolic_ems
fit$fit$variance_components$unrestricted

    derive_nested_ems() exposes the trace-derived numerator and denominator EMS. estimate_nested_variance_components() solves the hierarchy’s balanced EMS system and retains negative unrestricted estimates; truncate = TRUE adds a separate zero-truncated sensitivity result.

    Every term’s estimable projector must lie wholly in one stratum. Balanced cross-level interactions are supported when parameterized with orthogonal contrasts such as explicitly assigned contr.sum; otherwise the engine rejects the ambiguous projector and names that remedy. Contrasts are never changed silently because doing so could change the tested hypothesis.

    Balanced crossed-nested hybrid inference

    Phase 9 combines one nested hierarchy with explicitly declared treatment interactions:

    design <- compile_permanova_design(
  ~ treatment +
    (1 | region/site) +
    (1 | treatment:region) +
    (1 | treatment:region:site),
  data = sampling_design,
  distance = community_distance
)

hybrid <- permanova_hybrid(
  design,
  permutations = 9999,
  seed = 5
)

    The treatment numerator is tested over MS[treatment:region]. Permutations move complete treatment-by-region profiles within each region, carrying every nested site and replicate intact. The first hybrid envelope is deliberately exact: one treatment, one region/site hierarchy, complete treatment occurrence within every site, equal replication, and all treatment-by-hierarchy covariance components declared explicitly.

    Unbalanced fixed-effect inference

    Phase 10 makes the requested hypothesis explicit:

    fit <- permanova(
  community_distance ~ habitat + season,
  sampling_design,
  type = "II",
  permutations = 9999,
  seed = 5
)

    Type I tests follow formula order. Type II tests respect marginality: a main effect is adjusted for terms that do not contain it while its containing higher-order interactions are held out of that reduced model. Type III retains all other terms and requires a full-rank model; with interactions, assign explicit sum-to-zero contrasts such as contr.sum before compiling. derive_unbalanced_hypotheses() exposes df, nominal df, adjustment terms, aliases, and the projector before inference.

    Every selected term must be fully estimable and is tested over the final full-model residual mean square with its own Freedman–Lane permutation. Phase 10 does not infer an unbalanced mixed-model EMS denominator: any random effect causes an explicit failure.

    Unequal-replication random-intercept inference

    Phase 11 targets equally weighted whole-plot centroids when observation counts differ among random-intercept units:

    design <- compile_permanova_design(
  ~ treatment + (1 | site),
  data = sampling_design,
  distance = community_distance
)

fit <- permanova_unequal_random_intercept(
  design,
  permutations = 9999,
  seed = 5
)

    The pseudo-F uses a cluster-centroid residual denominator. Freedman–Lane residuals move only among whole clusters with the same observation count, and the size-stratified permutation action must span every treatment contrast. The result is a cluster-weighted empirical test. It is not an observation-weighted EMS approximation, and no parametric F p-value is reported.

    Unbalanced nested and randomized-block inference

    Phase 12 uses separate empirical engines for two different unit structures:

    nested_fit <- permanova_unbalanced_nested(
  compile_permanova_design(
    ~ treatment + (1 | region/site), sampling_design, community_distance
  ),
  permutations = 9999,
  seed = 5
)

block_fit <- permanova_unbalanced_block(
  compile_permanova_design(
    ~ treatment + (1 | block) + (1 | treatment:block),
    sampling_design, community_distance
  ),
  permutations = 9999,
  seed = 5
)

    The nested engine gives equal weight to top-unit centroids and permutes residuals only among identical sorted child observation-count topologies. The block engine gives equal weight to observed treatment-by-block cell centroids and permutes intact profiles only within block and exact cell size. In both cases the restricted permutation action must span every treatment contrast; otherwise the global hypothesis rejects before inference.

    Lower-level unbalanced nested inference

    Phase 25 handles a categorical treatment assigned below the parent in one unbalanced parent/child hierarchy:

    lower_fit <- permanova_unbalanced_nested_lower(
  compile_permanova_design(
    ~ treatment + (1 | region/site), sampling_design, community_distance
  ),
  level = "auto",
  permutations = 9999,
  seed = 5
)

    If treatment is constant within child, equally weighted child centroids are adjusted for parent and residuals move only among children in the same parent and exact-size stratum. If treatment varies within child, observations are adjusted for child and residuals move only within child. The same unit models are available to permanova_mixed_contrasts(), permanova_mixed_pairwise(), and the explicitly weak permanova_mixed_maxT() family. Parent-level treatment remains the existing topology-stratified top-unit problem.

    Unbalanced crossed-nested hybrid inference

    Phase 26 handles one treatment crossed with regions and sites nested within regions when site counts, profile incidence, or cell replication are unequal:

    hybrid_fit <- permanova_unbalanced_hybrid(
  compile_permanova_design(
    ~ treatment + (1 | region/site) +
      (1 | treatment:region) + (1 | treatment:region:site),
    sampling_design, community_distance
  ),
  permutations = 9999,
  seed = 5
)

    Each observed treatment-by-region profile must contain every site in that region. Observations are first averaged within treatment-by-site cells, then site-cell centroids receive equal weight in the profile. The treatment test is adjusted for region and uses the remaining profile-centroid mean square; inference is empirical and makes no unbalanced EMS claim. Intact profiles move only within region and the same ordered site-specific cell-count topology. Missing whole profiles are allowed when incidence remains connected and those restricted actions span every treatment contrast. Mixed planned/pairwise and weak complete-null max-F contrasts reuse the same profiles and a common region reference grid.

    Correlated random intercepts and slopes

    Phase 27 supports a balanced complete two-condition repeated-measures model:

    slope_fit <- permanova(
  community_distance ~ condition + (1 + condition | subject),
  repeated_design,
  permutations = "all",
  truncate = TRUE
)

    A continuous covariate slope, ~ x + (1 + x | group), routes instead to permanova_random_slope_continuous(), which aggregates to per-group slope vectors and reproduces the exact two-stage slope test.

    The random intercept is the subject midpoint under centred two-condition coding; the random slope is the complete second-minus-first condition difference vector. The fixed-effect pseudo-F tests the population mean difference over between-subject slope variation and equals a paired t statistic squared for a Euclidean scalar response. Inference sign-flips whole subject difference vectors and therefore requires central symmetry under the null; it is not described as unrestricted condition-label exchangeability. The reported trace covariance removes equal within-cell sampling noise by method of moments, retains negative unrestricted estimates, and optionally supplies a separate positive-semidefinite sensitivity.

    More than two conditions, incomplete subjects, unequal or unreplicated cells, extra fixed effects, and asymmetric difference distributions lie outside this contract. Non-Euclidean empirical inference is retained, but its Gaussian parametric p-value is suppressed.

    Planned contrasts and pairwise comparisons

    Phase 13 tests explicit one-df contrasts among the centroids of one categorical fixed factor, including unequal group sizes:

    planned <- rbind(
  `A - B` = c(A = 1, B = -1, C = 0),
  `AB - C` = c(A = 0.5, B = 0.5, C = -1)
)

planned_fit <- permanova_contrasts(
  design,
  contrasts = planned,
  adjust = "holm",
  permutations = 9999,
  seed = 5
)

pairwise_fit <- permanova_pairwise(
  design,
  adjust = "holm",
  permutations = 9999,
  seed = 5
)

    Contrast coefficients apply to unweighted group centroids and must sum to zero. Each contrast receives a reduced model that retains every orthogonal group-centroid direction plus its own Freedman–Lane permutation. Holm is the default multiplicity adjustment; Bonferroni, BH, BY, and no adjustment are available explicitly.

    Multifactor marginal contrasts

    Phase 15 defines how nuisance factors are averaged before testing a target- factor contrast:

    means <- derive_marginal_means(
  design, factor = "treatment", weights = "equal"
)

fit <- permanova_marginal_contrasts(
  design,
  factor = "treatment",
  contrasts = planned,
  weights = "equal",
  permutations = 9999,
  seed = 5
)

pairs <- permanova_marginal_pairwise(
  design,
  factor = "treatment",
  weights = "proportional",
  permutations = 9999,
  seed = 5
)

    Equal weights average the complete categorical nuisance grid. Proportional weights use observed joint nuisance-cell frequencies. The fixed model must be full rank and categorical. Random effects reject; use the explicit covariate- reference interface below when numeric predictors are present.

    Continuous-covariate adjusted contrasts

    Phase 20 tests fixed-model contrasts at user-declared numeric covariate values:

    means <- derive_adjusted_means(
  design, factor = "treatment", at = c(temperature = 20),
  weights = "equal"
)

fit <- permanova_adjusted_contrasts(
  design, factor = "treatment", contrasts = planned,
  at = c(temperature = 20), weights = "equal",
  permutations = 9999, seed = 5
)

pairs <- permanova_adjusted_pairwise(
  design, factor = "treatment", at = c(temperature = 20),
  weights = "proportional", permutations = 9999, seed = 5
)

    Every ordinary numeric nuisance covariate requires one named finite scalar in at; none is inferred from the observations. Categorical nuisance factors are averaged over an equal reference grid or observed joint frequencies. Random effects, aliased or ill-conditioned fixed models, unsupported predictor classes, and incomplete reference specifications reject explicitly. The adjusted-mean result reports fixed_model_condition_ratio; models whose ratio cannot support stable information-matrix construction at tol reject before projector construction.

    Mixed-design contrasts

    Phase 16 tests treatment contrasts on the experimental-unit scale selected by the declared balanced random structure:

    fit <- permanova_mixed_contrasts(
  design,
  contrasts = planned,
  adjust = "holm",
  permutations = 9999,
  seed = 5
)

pairs <- permanova_mixed_pairwise(
  design, adjust = "holm", permutations = 9999, seed = 5
)

    One random intercept uses equally weighted whole-unit centroids; a top-level nested treatment uses intact top-unit centroids; a declared randomized block uses treatment-by-block cell centroids; and the balanced region/site hybrid uses treatment-by-region profiles. Unequal unit sizes restrict whole-unit residuals by exact size, unbalanced nested units by complete topology, and incomplete block cells jointly by block and exact cell size. Incomplete blocks use one common block reference grid for treatment means. Treatments assigned below the top of an unbalanced hierarchy remain explicit failures.

    Global-null max-F contrasts

    Phase 17 uses one shared raw-observation permutation distribution for a fixed one-factor contrast family:

    fit <- permanova_maxT(
  design, contrasts = planned, permutations = 9999, seed = 5
)

pairs <- permanova_maxT_pairwise(
  design, permutations = 9999, seed = 5
)

    Each permutation contributes the largest contrast pseudo-F. p_maxT compares each observed statistic with those maxima. The guarantee is deliberately limited to weak familywise error control under the complete equal-centroid null. Strong subset-null control is not claimed by this engine.

    Strong closed pairwise inference

    Phase 28 provides a narrower family for which subset-null exchangeability can be proved:

    pairs <- permanova_pairwise_strong(
  design, permutations = 9999, seed = 5
)

    For every intersection of pairwise equalities, factor levels joined by those equalities form connected components. Observations are reassigned only within each component while preserving group sizes; non-null groups remain fixed. Under independent observations and equality of the complete distributions inside each component, this raw-label action leaves the intersection-null law invariant. A maximum pseudo-F tests the intersection, and closed testing gives p_closed strong FWER without invoking subset pivotality.

    The distinction is substantive: this is not a strong-control claim for equal centroids when dispersions or distribution shapes differ. Planned non-pairwise contrasts, dependent observations, repeated measures, and mixed designs remain unsupported by the strong engine.

    Mixed-design global-null max-F contrasts

    Phase 21 carries the same complete-null maximum-statistic contract to the experimental-unit scale of supported mixed designs:

    fit <- permanova_mixed_maxT(
  design, contrasts = planned, permutations = 9999, seed = 5
)

pairs <- permanova_mixed_maxT_pairwise(
  design, permutations = 9999, seed = 5
)

    One shared raw experimental-unit permutation stream is used across every contrast. Balanced whole units move intact; unequal units remain within exact size strata; unbalanced nested top units remain within topology strata; and block or hybrid profiles remain within the corresponding block, block-by-size, or region strata. p_maxT provides weak FWER under the complete treatment-null randomization hypothesis. It does not provide strong subset-null control.

    V2 support registry

    Phase 22 consolidates the public inference contract without broadening any runtime support envelope:

    permanova_capabilities()

    Each row names a primary engine and its validated design, estimand, denominator, permutation contract, error-control claim, and explicit exclusions. The human-readable companion is inst/SUPPORT-MATRIX.md. These maps aid discovery; the compiler and each engine’s runtime validator remain authoritative for a particular design.

    Calibration hardening

    Phase 14 audits unequal-random-intercept inference against the exact unique treatment-label randomization distribution across independent seed batches:

    calibration_audit <- audit_unequal_random_intercept_calibration(
  batches = 20,
  simulations_per_batch = 500,
  permutations = 99,
  engine_checks = 10,
  seed = 20260719
)

marginal_validation <- simulate_marginal_contrast_validation(
  simulations = 500,
  permutations = 99,
  seed = 20260719
)

    Release readiness

    The source tree is the 0.9.0.9000 pre-release development version. The next stable version is 1.0.0; no tag or submission is implied by development checks. See inst/RELEASE-HANDOFF.md for the owner-only publication boundary. The package version policy is recorded in inst/VERSIONING.md.

    The structural audit, test suite, source build, and package check are reproducible locally:

    Rscript tools/release-audit.R
Rscript -e 'testthat::test_local(reporter = "progress")'
R CMD build .
R CMD check --no-manual distmer_0.9.0.9000.tar.gz

    Hosted CI repeats an --as-cran check on Linux, macOS, and Windows. The audit reports publication metadata separately from technical package integrity; set STRICT_RELEASE_METADATA=true to make unresolved metadata fatal. See inst/RELEASE-READINESS.md for the exact handoff gate.

    The current gate covers the deterministic validation battery, complete source test suite, all seven consolidated vignettes, source build, and installed package check. Results are recorded only after those commands have run against the active version; retired Phase artifacts are not treated as evidence for the development tree.

    The audit separates 13,824 distinct profile rearrangements from 216 unique labels in the canonical balanced-allocation example, verifies identical exact p-values, and records seed ranges spaced one million apart. Exchangeable Gaussian, heavy-tail, and unequal-allocation nulls determine the calibration gate. Treatment-specific dispersion is reported only as a violated- exchangeability sensitivity.

    Design-aware multivariate dispersion

    permanova_dispersion() tests whether mean distances to group spatial medians or centroids differ while retaining the design’s exact EMS denominator and restricted exchangeability units:

    design <- compile_permanova_design(
  ~ treatment + (1 | block) + (1 | treatment:block),
  data = sampling_design,
  distance = community_distance
)

dispersion <- permanova_dispersion(
  design,
  term = "treatment",
  type = "median",
  permutations = 9999,
  seed = 5
)

    The original positive and negative principal-coordinate axes are retained. The default spatial median has materially better small-sample null calibration than the centroid in the pinned validation; centroid results remain available as an explicit sensitivity. Phase 8 requires a design containing exactly one categorical fixed main effect with equal target-group sizes. A significant dispersion result can complicate interpretation of a location test, while a non-significant result does not prove exchangeability.

  simulations = 500,

)

benchmark_permanova(
  group_counts = c(8, 16, 32),
  permutations = c(99, 999)
)

    Simulation output includes Monte Carlo uncertainty, denominator agreement, failure counts, dispersion sensitivity, and runtime. Benchmark results are machine-specific measurements, not universal performance claims. See the package vignette for supported-design boundaries and interpretation.

    Vignette series

    The guide begins with ordinary ecological questions and introduces the implementation detail only when random effects make it useful.

    • Getting started with distmer (vignette("getting-started")): what a distance-based mixed model is, how it relates to PERMANOVA, and a first vegan::dune analysis;
    • Fixed effects: Type I, II, and III (vignette("fixed-effects")): choosing an estimable fixed-effect question with the vegan::mite data;
    • Pairwise contrasts and multiple comparisons (vignette("contrasts")): planned, pairwise, marginal, and covariate-adjusted comparisons using dune;
    • Dispersion and distance diagnostics (vignette("dispersion")): distance geometry, design-aware dispersion, and vegan::betadisper() agreement;
    • Unbalanced designs (vignette("unbalanced-mixed")): unequal fixed cells, missed repeated visits, unit weighting, and restricted permutations;
    • Random effects and ecological sampling designs (vignette("random-effects")): repeated sites, nesting, blocks, hybrids, random slopes, and the specialised implementation reference;
    • Validation and reproducibility (vignette("validation")): reference agreement, deterministic checks, simulations, and a reporting checklist.

    Example 

    library(distmer)

Y <- matrix(
  c(
    0, 0,
    0, 1,
    1, 0,
    4, 4,
    4, 5,
    5, 4
  ),
  ncol = 2,
  byrow = TRUE
)

group <- factor(rep(c("A", "B"), each = 3))
D <- dist(Y)

permanova_oneway(
  distance = D,
  group = group,
  permutations = 9999,
  seed = 5,
  engine = "pairwise"
)

    Multi-factor development engine 

    dat <- expand.grid(
  treatment = factor(c("control", "impact")),
  block = factor(seq_len(4)),
  replicate = seq_len(3)
)

set.seed(1)
Y <- matrix(rpois(nrow(dat) * 8, lambda = 4), ncol = 8)
D <- dist(Y)

permanova_fixed(
  distance = D,
  formula = ~ treatment * block,
  data = dat,
  permutations = 999,
  seed = 5
)

    The permanova_fixed() function tests all terms over residual and therefore must not itself be used for random, nested, repeated, or mixed designs. Use the dedicated mixed engines only within their documented support boundaries.
